# `silk/time/instant`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Points in time: the [`Instant`](#Instant) type, a moment on the UTC timeline with nanosecond precision.

## When to use

Use [`Instant`](#Instant) for when something happened or will happen, the same for every observer: a
timestamp in a log, an expiry, the time a file changed. `SystemClock.now` in
`silk.system.system_clock` reads the current one. To show an instant to a person, convert it
with [`Instant.toUtc`](#Instant.impl.toUtc) or [`Instant.toOffset`](#Instant.impl.toOffset).

## Details

An `Instant` counts seconds and nanoseconds from the Unix epoch, `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`, and
ignores leap seconds, as Unix time does. The range is 100 million days in each direction,
`-271821-04-20T00:00:00Z` to `+275760-09-13T00:00:00Z`, the range of ECMAScript Temporal.

`instant + duration` and `instant - duration` move along the timeline, and
`instant - instant` gives the `Duration` between two points.

## Examples

### Parse a timestamp, add a span, and print it

```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.duration { Duration }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.text { TimeParseError }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  match Instant.parse("2026-11-19T18:36:22+01:00") {
    Result<Instant, TimeParseError>.Success { value } => {
      if value.unixSeconds() != 1795109782 {
        return 1
      }
      let later = value + Duration.fromHours(7)
      let reading = later.toUtc()
      if reading.date().day() != 20 || reading.time().hour() != 0 {
        return 2
      }
      if &(later - value) != &Duration.fromSeconds(25200) {
        return 3
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<Instant, TimeParseError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 4
    }
  }
}
```

Import as `Instant` with `import silk.time.instant { Instant }`.

## `Instant`

```silk
pub struct Instant
```

A point on the UTC timeline with nanosecond precision.

### Details

The value is whole seconds since `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`, rounded toward negative infinity, and
a nanosecond part from 0 to 999,999,999 that counts forward, also before 1970. Leap seconds
are not counted, as in Unix time. The range is `-271821-04-20T00:00:00Z` to
`+275760-09-13T00:00:00Z`.

`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare positions on the timeline. `+` and `-` with a
`Duration` move the instant and trap when the result is outside the range. `-` between two
instants gives a `Duration`. `Display` writes the reading in UTC with the suffix `Z`.

<a id="Instant.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(seconds: i64, nanoseconds: i64) -> Instant
```

Returns the instant `seconds` seconds plus `nanoseconds` nanoseconds after the Unix epoch.

#### Details

Whole seconds in `nanoseconds` move into the seconds, and both arguments can be negative. So
`Instant.make(0, 5000000000)` is five seconds after the epoch and `Instant.make(0, -1)` is
one nanosecond before it.

#### Gotchas

An instant outside the range traps. [`Instant.checkedMake`](#Instant.impl.checkedMake) returns `None` instead.

<a id="Instant.impl.checkedMake"></a>


Returns the instant `seconds` seconds plus `nanoseconds` nanoseconds after the Unix epoch, or
`None` when it is outside `-271821-04-20T00:00:00Z` to `+275760-09-13T00:00:00Z`.

#### Details

Whole seconds in `nanoseconds` move into the seconds, and both arguments can be negative.

<a id="Instant.impl.unixSeconds"></a>

### Method `unixSeconds`

```silk
pub fn unixSeconds(self: Self) -> i64
```

Returns the whole seconds since the Unix epoch, rounded toward negative infinity.

#### Details

The instant is this value plus [`Instant.subsecondNanoseconds`](#Instant.impl.subsecondNanoseconds). Half a second before the
epoch has `-1` whole seconds and a nanosecond part of 500,000,000.

<a id="Instant.impl.round"></a>

### Method `round`

```silk
pub fn round(self: Self, step: TimeIncrement, mode: RoundingMode) -> Instant
```

Returns the instant rounded to a multiple of `step`, counted from the Unix epoch.

#### Details

The steps are those of the time of day in UTC. An instant is a point and not an amount, so
"away from zero" means later in time, also before 1970: `RoundingMode.Expand` rounds as
`Ceil` and `HalfExpand` as `HalfCeil`.

#### Gotchas

A result outside the range traps. [`Instant.checkedRound`](#Instant.impl.checkedRound) returns `None` instead.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.rounding { RoundingMode, TimeIncrement, TimeUnit }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let at = Instant.make(1795000000, 250000000)
  let second = at.round(TimeIncrement.one(TimeUnit.Second), RoundingMode.HalfExpand)
  if second.unixSeconds() != 1795000000 || second.subsecondNanoseconds() != 0 {
    return 1
  }
  let hour = at.round(TimeIncrement.one(TimeUnit.Hour), RoundingMode.Ceil)
  if hour.unixSeconds() != 1795003200 {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Instant.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<Instant, TimeParseError>
```

Reads an instant from RFC 3339 or ISO 8601 text such as `2026-11-19T17:36:22.5Z`.

#### Details

The text is a date, `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYYMMDD`, then `T`, `t`, or a space, then a time:
`HH`, `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, `HHMM`, or `HHMMSS`, with an optional fraction of one to nine
digits, then `Z` or a numeric offset such as `+01:00`. Second `60` reads as `59`. Bracketed
annotations can follow, as in `2026-11-19T18:36:22+01:00[Europe/Rome]`. They are checked and
then ignored: the offset alone decides the instant.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as month 13 or hour 24,
  or the instant is outside the range.
- `TimeParseReason.MissingTime` if the text has no time of day.
- `TimeParseReason.MissingOffset` if the text has neither `Z` nor a numeric offset.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.

- `TimeParseReason.MissingTime` if the text has no time of day.

- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.

<a id="Instant.impl.writeUtc"></a>

### Method `writeUtc`

```silk
pub fn writeUtc(self: Self, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes the instant as the reading in UTC with the suffix `Z`, as in `2026-11-19T17:36:22Z`,
at `output[at]`, and returns the offset after it.

#### Details

The text is valid RFC 3339 for the years 0 to 9999. It has a fraction, without zeros at the
end, when the nanosecond part is not zero. It is at most 33 bytes.

<a id="Instant.impl.writeWithOffset"></a>

### Method `writeWithOffset`

```silk
pub fn writeWithOffset(self: Self, offset: UtcOffset, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes the instant as the reading of a clock `offset` ahead of UTC, followed by that offset,
as in `2026-11-19T18:36:22+01:00`, at `output[at]`, and returns the offset after it.

#### Details

The text is valid RFC 3339 for the years 0 to 9999 when the offset has no seconds part. The
zero offset is written `+00:00`. The text is at most 41 bytes.
